db_evidence.notes: The literal item name 佛目珠 and the boss name 石母 never appear as text in episodes, event_steps, topic_facts, or visual_clips (every LIKE '%佛目珠%'/'%石母%' query across all 5 rollouts returned 0 rows), so this is not a text-searchable fact -- it can only be established by visually sampling the on-screen Chinese pickup-notification toast via clip_qa. The captioned episode/event_steps text does describe the surrounding action generically enough (stone-head/stone-face interactions, 'item pickup notification appearing', 'defeated enemy collapses into a giant stone face') to localize all 5 candidate windows textually, and 3 of the 5 rollouts (00, 01, 03) retrieved that text but still failed to convert all 5 candidate windows into clip_qa calls.

root_causes: The ground-truth item name and boss name are never present as searchable text in the DB; success depends entirely on how thoroughly and how densely the visual sub-agent (clip_qa) is used across the full pre-boss span.

Rollouts 0/1/3 stopped short of full temporal coverage: they either anchored on a small number of self-picked candidate timestamps from an early pass (01, 03, missing 2 of 5 windows) or checked only the single window right before the boss fight (00, missing 4 of 5 windows), even though their own SQL dumps of the 30sec episode captions already showed pickup-adjacent events in the unchecked windows.

Rollout 4's failure was a visual-sampling-density issue rather than a coverage issue: it covered the full span but in one clip_qa call spanning ~1190s, and the sub-agent under-sampled frames and missed one distinct pickup that a narrower two-call split (rollout 2) caught.

Rollout 2 succeeded by splitting the same overall span into two moderate clip_qa windows (~750s and ~600s), giving the visual sub-agent enough frame density per call to catch every one of the 5 toast events.
what_worked: Rollout 2's strategy of first localizing the pre-boss span from event_steps/episodes text, then splitting that span into two clip_qa calls of moderate length (not one wide call, not many overly narrow calls) so the visual sub-agent could densely sample frames within each.
Explicitly asking clip_qa to distinguish an actual 佛目珠 pickup toast from mere stone-head inspection or other loot, which avoided over-counting from duplicate/lingering toasts.
transferable_lessons: For on-screen-text/counting questions where the target string never appears in the DB's captioned text, do not rely on semantic_search/run_sql to find the exact events -- use them only to localize the approximate time span, then hand the full span to clip_qa.

When calling clip_qa for a counting question, split a long candidate span into a small number of moderate-length windows (a few hundred to ~750s) rather than one very wide window or many very narrow hand-picked windows; very wide windows under-sample frames and merge/drop events, while narrow windows chosen from an incomplete first pass silently skip whole candidate intervals.

Before finalizing 3 or fewer clip_qa calls for a 'count total occurrences over an interval' question, double-check that every anomalous or pickup-adjacent episode already surfaced by earlier SQL/semantic_search (e.g. 'item pickup notification appearing', 'stone face collapses') has been assigned to some clip_qa window -- don't stop at the first few visually-confirmed hits.
Treat a rejected clip_qa call (interval too long) as a signal to bisect the interval into 2 balanced windows, not to just shrink to one maximal allowed window that may still be too coarse.
open_questions: The reference clue_interval [11867, 11842] has end < start, which looks like a data entry error in the question/annotation file; it is unclear which corrected interval (e.g. 11842-11867) it was meant to represent, though this did not appear to affect any rollout's behavior.

It was not directly confirmed via frame inspection (only via clip_qa's own textual answer) that the 12540.5s and 12887s events are genuinely two separate, non-duplicate 佛目珠 pickups rather than one lingering toast split across two sampled frames; this rests on trusting the visual sub-agent's own dedup judgement in rollout 2.
